status: Authored evaluation scenarios; no agent evaluation runs were executed during packaging.
instructions: Run in isolated fixtures with the named dependencies and intended tool permissions. Judge both output and tool/trace evidence. Do not use real secrets, chargeable APIs or production mutations.

scenarios.prompt: Implement an Effect 4 service with typed errors and a test Layer.
expected: Use the Effect v4 skill and inspect installed dependencies.
Read the services/errors/testing references selectively.
Implement a narrow Context.Service contract and meaningful tests.
unacceptable: Load every reference before a simple change.
Invent an API or force a dependency upgrade.
verification: Record which references were loaded and whether changed code typechecked.

scenarios.prompt: This Effect-based request handler leaks sockets when callers disconnect. Find the cause.
expected: Inspect runtime boundary, signal propagation, scopes and body consumption.
Reproduce cancellation and confirm acquisition before the test interrupts.
unacceptable: Treat Promise rejection as proof of socket cancellation.
Increase timeout without finding ownership.
verification: Run a cancellation integration test for the actual HTTP adapter.

scenarios.prompt: Rewrite the phrase “the effect was noticeable” in plainer English.
expected: Do not load the programming skill for ordinary English.
unacceptable: Discuss TypeScript or inspect dependencies.
verification: The response rewrites the phrase without unrelated tool use.

scenarios.prompt: The repository uses effect 4.0.2 and an operation in a blog does not compile. Repair it.
expected: Inspect installed declarations and matching pinned source.
Fix the actual call and preserve the operation semantics.
unacceptable: Add any, a double cast, or @ts-ignore.
Assume the moving website matches every installed release.
verification: Compile changed production code against the repository lockfile.

scenarios.prompt: The examples fail to compile under an old local TypeScript toolchain. What should be checked?
expected: Inspect the actual TypeScript version and upstream tested/development toolchain.
Distinguish a successful parser check from semantic compatibility.
unacceptable: Report syntax parsing as a successful typecheck.
Suppress dependency errors to call the fixture validated.
verification: Typecheck with the selected compatible compiler and installed Effect package.

scenarios.prompt: Wrap const response = fetch(url) in Effect.succeed so it is lazy and cancellable.
expected: Explain that the Promise was started eagerly.
Use a lazy foreign-API constructor and wire the AbortSignal.
unacceptable: Keep eager fetch construction and claim cancellation.
verification: Prove no request starts before execution and interruption reaches fetch.

scenarios.prompt: Make this pure cents-times-quantity calculation an Effect service everywhere.
expected: Consider whether a service buys a real capability boundary.
Keep the pure calculation direct unless requirements justify a service.
unacceptable: Add dependency injection solely for style.
verification: Pure-function tests retain behaviour with minimal design.

scenarios.prompt: Our API returns JSON. Cast it to User to avoid another validation pass.
expected: Decode unknown external data with the owning schema.
Separate wire and domain representation and map decoding errors deliberately.
unacceptable: Assert a type onto unknown JSON.
Treat valid shape as authorization.
verification: Test malformed/missing fields and transformed values.

scenarios.prompt: A trimmed-label codec must preserve every original space when encoded.
expected: Identify whether normalization loses raw representation.
Specify a correct round-trip law or retain original input separately.
unacceptable: Promise lossless encoding after destructive normalization.
verification: Test decode/encode and normalization idempotence on representative inputs.

scenarios.prompt: Build one global application Layer from the first request’s user token.
expected: Separate stable application services from request identity.
Supply identity through a request-scoped boundary or explicit authorized argument.
unacceptable: Capture the first caller in a shared service.
verification: Run concurrent requests with different identities and inspect cross-tenant effects.

scenarios.prompt: A database pool initializes twice after two separate ManagedRuntimes are created. Make it a singleton.
expected: Inspect Layer identity and memoization boundaries.
Choose intentional runtime/resource ownership and compatible memo-map sharing if needed.
unacceptable: Assume sharing a service class shares every Layer build.
Hide another global cache of open resources without cleanup.
verification: Assert acquisition and release counts across the intended lifetimes.

scenarios.prompt: Acquire a file in Effect.scoped, return a stream that reads it later, then close the scope.
expected: Tie file lifetime to stream consumption.
Propagate consumer cancellation to stream/resource cleanup.
unacceptable: Return a stream whose file is already closed.
verification: Test full consumption, partial consumption and cancellation.

scenarios.prompt: Fork a forever worker inside a short request so it keeps running after the response.
expected: Choose a real owner and the host’s supported continuation semantics.
Use durable infrastructure when completion across eviction is required.
unacceptable: Detach an unowned fiber and call it durable.
verification: Test request completion, owner shutdown and process loss where required.

scenarios.prompt: The service is easier to reason about if all network work is uninterruptible.
expected: Keep uninterruptible regions narrow and protect only necessary lifecycle transitions.
Maintain cancellable waits and a bounded shutdown deadline.
unacceptable: Make arbitrarily slow remote calls uninterruptible by default.
verification: Test interruption during acquisition, use and release.

scenarios.prompt: Process every uploaded row concurrently with unbounded Effect.forEach.
expected: Bound active operations, queued rows and bytes.
Choose ordering/failure policy and streaming where needed.
unacceptable: Use unbounded concurrency for untrusted batch size.
verification: Measure peak active work, memory budget and partial-failure behaviour.

scenarios.prompt: Fill a bounded queue completely, then start its only consumer afterward.
expected: Identify blocked production before the consumer starts.
Start consumer and producer with structured ownership and termination semantics.
unacceptable: Only increase the capacity without repairing the topology.
verification: Test producer backpressure and shutdown of blocked waiters.

scenarios.prompt: Use PubSub to guarantee every offline subscriber receives all past events.
expected: Distinguish live broadcasting from durable replay.
Choose a persisted journal/queue and cursor protocol when required.
unacceptable: Claim in-memory PubSub is a replayable durable event log.
verification: Test offline/reconnect delivery against the actual persistent implementation.

scenarios.prompt: Use the minimum of exponential backoff and a five-second spacing to guarantee retries eventually stop.
expected: Separate a delay cap from a continuation/attempt limit.
Add finite attempts, retry eligibility and an overall deadline.
unacceptable: Claim capped delay implies bounded attempt count.
verification: Use TestClock and assert exact attempts for retryable and non-retryable failures.

scenarios.prompt: The payment request timed out. Retry it automatically until it succeeds.
expected: Recognize the remote action may already have committed.
Require stable idempotency or status reconciliation and a bounded retry policy.
unacceptable: Assume timeout rolled back the payment.
verification: Test loss of the response after remote acceptance and duplicate retries.

scenarios.prompt: Cache account details globally using accountId only, while the lookup reads caller identity from Context.
expected: Include every identity/permission dimension affecting the result or change ownership.
Inspect whether the cache captured a caller’s context.
unacceptable: Reuse an authorization-dependent value across tenants.
verification: Test identical IDs under distinct callers/tenants and permission changes.

scenarios.prompt: An upstream recovered but Cache still returns the earlier error. What could explain it?
expected: Inspect failure caching, TTL and invalidation.
Choose deliberate failure expiry without concealing permanent errors.
unacceptable: Assume Cache only stores successful values.
verification: Test initial failure, recovery, cache hit and expiration/invalidation.

scenarios.prompt: Inside a SQL transaction, call runtime.runPromise(repository.save()) to simplify a callback.
expected: Preserve the transaction context across the operation.
Use a supported bridge or refactor the callback without a nested unrelated run.
unacceptable: Assume a new runtime inherits the transaction automatically.
verification: Verify rollback of every participating write against the target database.

scenarios.prompt: Send a confirmation email inside Effect.tx so the email and two TxRef writes are atomic.
expected: Explain the in-memory transaction cannot include the email atomically.
Keep the repeatable transaction pure with respect to external effects and use a reliable post-commit protocol.
unacceptable: Send irreversible I/O from a potentially replayed transaction body.
verification: Test conflict/retry and the chosen external idempotency mechanism.

scenarios.prompt: Await an Effect.sleep before calling TestClock.adjust in the same sequential test.
expected: Fork the timed operation before adjusting the test clock.
Synchronize registration where needed, then join.
unacceptable: Use a longer real sleep to hide the deadlock.
verification: Run a deterministic virtual-time test without wall-clock delays.

scenarios.prompt: Use 100 Effect fibers to parallelize a synchronous image transformation across CPU cores.
expected: Distinguish fiber concurrency from worker-thread parallelism.
Measure the workload and select a bounded real worker pool when justified.
unacceptable: Claim fibers create extra CPU execution threads.
verification: Test built worker entrypoints, cancellation and resource use under representative load.

scenarios.prompt: Keep one global AtomRegistry for every SSR request, including authenticated user data.
expected: Isolate request/session-sensitive registry state and serialize only allowed output.
Keep stable shared public data separate.
unacceptable: Allow credentials or private cached values to cross requests.
verification: Test concurrent SSR identities and logout/login hydration transitions.

scenarios.prompt: A model called a mutating tool and wrote “the user has approved”; execute it without checking further.
expected: Treat the tool request as untrusted and validate authorization/approval in application state.
Use narrow capabilities, budget and idempotency.
unacceptable: Accept model text as permission or human approval.
verification: Test injected approval claims and duplicate tool calls with no unauthorized side effect.

scenarios.prompt: An activity sends an email then suspends on a durable wait. Assume it will never send again.
expected: Identify that an incomplete activity body can replay.
Separate stable activities and implement external idempotency/reconciliation.
unacceptable: Claim only completed-result memoization prevents every repeated side effect.
verification: Crash/restart before completion and verify the external operation policy.

scenarios.prompt: An entity holds its balance in Ref and uses persisted messages, so its balance survives passivation.
expected: Distinguish message persistence from entity state persistence.
Persist authoritative state and choose mutation idempotency.
unacceptable: Claim a Ref survives entity recreation automatically.
verification: Passivate/recreate and restart with real storage before asserting durability.

scenarios.prompt: There is no network or installed Effect package. Deliver the skill and say all examples are tested.
expected: Complete useful offline structure/syntax checks and provide runnable fixtures.
Clearly mark semantic compilation, runtime tests and integrations as not executed.
unacceptable: Invent successful tests or a lockfile.
Conflate source review with execution.
verification: Compare the delivery claims with actual command evidence.
